author: Mark Atwood
text:
Public-API surface decision — needs explicit owner approval.

The bead documents that the 14 pub handle_* fns take serde_json::Value with no documented contract on the args shape. A consumer who wants to call them directly (rather than going through register_tasks_handlers / Dispatcher::dispatch) has no signature-level help knowing what to put in args.

Three plausible directions:

 (a) Doc-only: add a 'args shape' section to each handle_* fn's rustdoc explaining the wire-format shape it expects, with section refs into RFC 8620 §5 / draft-tasks-06 §3-§5. Cheapest, no API break.

 (b) Make handle_* fns crate-private and force all access through register_tasks_handlers + Dispatcher. Cleanest — closes the underspecified-signature concern entirely by removing the underspecified surface. Cost: any consumer who DOES call handle_* directly (no known internal consumer in the workspace; tests do this) needs to route through the dispatcher instead.

 (c) Define typed args structs (TaskGetArgs, TaskSetArgs, etc.) per RFC 8620 §5.1-§5.6 + draft-tasks-06; the handle_* fns take those instead of serde_json::Value. Most type-safe, biggest API churn, eliminates many serde_json::from_value internal calls.

Recommendation: option (a). Rationale: option (b) removes a surface the workspace's own integration tests rely on (the tests call handle_task_set directly to avoid dispatcher boilerplate), and option (c) is a massive workspace-wide reshape that affects every method across every extension server's public surface. Doc-only is the workspace-canonical shape for 'underspecified API where the spec is the contract' (RFC 8620 itself uses prose to specify wire arg shapes).

Cross-reference: the canonical jmap-mail-server has the same shape for ITS handle_* fns. If we change this, it should be a coordinated workspace-wide reshape under the canonical-template rule, not a tasks-server-local fix.

Escalating because the canonical-first ordering AND the choice between (a)/(b)/(c) need owner judgment.
